candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — contraindications and medication safety
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fondaparinux renal safety
candidate.educational_objective: Identify severe renal impairment as a contraindication to fondaparinux for VTE prophylaxis/treatment.

options.A: Administer the medication because renal function does not materially affect fondaparinux clearance
options.B: Question the order because fondaparinux is contraindicated for VTE prophylaxis or treatment when CrCl is less than 30 mL/min
options.C: Administer the medication intramuscularly to reduce accumulation in renal impairment
options.D: Double the dose because severe renal impairment reduces the anticoagulant effect of fondaparinux

candidate.rationale: Fondaparinux is substantially eliminated by the kidneys. Current labeling contraindicates VTE prophylaxis/treatment when CrCl is below 30 mL/min because reduced clearance increases anticoagulant exposure and bleeding risk. It is given subcutaneously, not intramuscularly.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Fondaparinux is contraindicated for VTE prophylaxis/treatment when CrCl is less than 30 mL/min.
candidate.source_locator: Sections 4, 5.3 and 8.6 — CrCl <30 mL/min contraindicated; reduced renal clearance increases bleeding risk
candidate.stem: An adult client with a creatinine clearance of 24 mL/min has a new order for fondaparinux for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after surgery. Which action should the nurse take?
